known_cause: The Brazilian real strengthened sharply (dollar down about 2%, back under R$4) after an election poll showed Bolsonaro gaining, and arabica rallied with it; short-covering added to the move.
notes: Closing report dated 2018-10-02: Dec/18 +545 points, which is +5.33%. Agrolink's report of the same day gives the same prices and the poll.

known_cause: Another sharp fall of the dollar against the real ahead of the election run-off lifted arabica, with buy orders triggered once the price cleared 120 cents.
notes: Closing report dated 2018-10-17: Dec/18 +490 points (+4.16%), dollar -1.05%. Canal Rural of 2018-10-18 gives the same cause.

known_cause: The day after Bolsonaro's election win the dollar rose against the real, which set off a reversal, a break below 120 cents and heavy profit-taking.
notes: Report dated 2018-10-30 on the previous session: Dec/18 -5.40 cents (-4.5%). Profit-taking is cited too, but a currency trigger is named. The size of the dollar move is not given.

known_cause: Only profit-taking after recent gains is given as the reason, with a vague mention of the exchange rate on a day the dollar closed flat.
notes: CHECK: borderline. Report dated 2018-11-30: Dec/18 -525 points (-4.84%). It says the market 'followed the exchange rate', but the dollar ended the day unchanged. If that mention counts as a cause, this becomes EXPLAIN.

known_cause: The dollar hit a three-week high against the real on fears the pension reform would be delayed, and the ICO raised its estimate of the global surplus; arabica fell to 2004 lows.
notes: Closing report dated 2019-04-17: May/19 -345 points (-3.81%). The midday report and a currency report of the same day agree.

known_cause: The report puts the rebound down to a technical recovery after the slide to 2004 lows together with a firmer real.
notes: CHECK: borderline. Closing report dated 2019-04-18: May/19 +315 points (+3.62%). The currency is named in the headline, but the dollar fell only 0.10% that day and the first reason given is a technical recovery. Read strictly this is REFUSE.

known_cause: Only a pause and profit-taking after four straight weeks of gains is reported; no event is named.
notes: Closing report dated 2019-11-11: Dec/19 -345 points (-3.15%). The dollar fell against the real that day, which would support coffee, so it does not explain the fall. Only one report for the day was found.

known_cause: A USDA report cut its estimate of Brazil's 2019/20 crop by about 10% to 58 million bags, and prices jumped.
notes: Closing report dated 2019-11-21: Dec/19 +555 points (+5.06%). The analyst quoted is slightly hedged: the USDA figures 'may have' driven the gains.

known_cause: Heavy rain in Minas Gerais and Espirito Santo was seen boosting Brazil's coming crop, and coronavirus store closures in China raised demand worries.
notes: Closing report dated 2020-02-03: Mar/20 -475 points (-4.63%). The midday report and the next morning's report give the same reasons.

known_cause: The report attributes the surge to positions being covered ahead of Brazil's Carnival holiday and to excess rain in Minas Gerais that could cut output, amplified by buying when the price broke 110 cents.
notes: CHECK: borderline. Closing report dated 2020-02-21: Mar/20 +525 points (+5.07%). The headline names weather and the holiday, but the analyst quoted says there were no fundamental reasons, only chart ones. Read strictly this is REFUSE.

known_cause: Hurricane Iota was approaching Central America's coffee regions two weeks after Hurricane Eta; dry weather in Brazil and a weaker dollar added support.
notes: Closing report dated 2020-11-16: Dec/20 +640 points (+5.86%). The midday report and a Bloomberg piece of the same day agree.

known_cause: A ten-day forecast pointed to heavier rain over Brazil's drought-hit coffee areas, and profit-taking after the late-November rally added to the fall.
notes: Closing report dated 2020-12-01: Mar/21 -485 points (about -3.9%, against -4.18% in the price series, which was probably still on the expiring December contract). Three reports name the rain forecast.

known_cause: Not a real move of this size: the price series switched from the expired March contract to May on this day. The May contract rose about 0.85%, which reports put down to below-average rain in Minas Gerais.
notes: CHECK: probable contract-roll artefact. Closing report dated 2021-03-22: May/21 +110 points to 130.10; the report of 2021-03-19 has May/21 at 129.00. The March contract's last trading day works out as 2021-03-19 (calculated from the exchange's rules, not confirmed from a source). Decide whether this date stays in the set.

known_cause: The rapid spread of the Omicron variant hit commodity and share markets and cut risk appetite; funds reduced long positions.
notes: Reuters report republished on 2021-12-20: March arabica -4.5%. The next day's Safras report gives the same cause.

known_cause: Arabica fell to a 15-month low on demand worries (inflation, interest rates, recession), with news of new Covid lockdowns in China that day, and funds selling on expectations of a large Brazil crop after good rain and flowering.
notes: Closing report dated 2022-10-28: Dec/22 -905 points (-5.06%). Most of the causes are conditions of several weeks; the China lockdown news is the one tied to the day.

known_cause: Speculation that Brazil's crop agency would cut its production estimate that week because of bad weather, with renewed concern about the 2023 crop and a rise in crude oil.
notes: Closing report dated 2022-12-12: Mar/23 +890 points (+5.63%, against +5.45% in the price series). Safras of the same day gives oil and crop worries.

known_cause: Not a real move of this size: the price series switched from the expired March contract to May on this day. The May contract fell about 1.3%; reports disagree on why (favourable weather and rising exchange stocks, or profit-taking before the US rate decision).
notes: CHECK: probable contract-roll artefact. Three reports of 2023-03-22 give May/23 -230 points to 178.00; the report of the day before has May/23 at 180.30. The March contract's last trading day works out as 2023-03-21 (calculated, not confirmed from a source). Decide whether this date stays in the set.

known_cause: Fund buying as the El Nino weather pattern was declared under way, which could hurt global coffee production.
notes: CHECK: sources conflict. Closing report dated 2023-06-08: Jul/23 +945 points (+5.09%). A broker's report of the same day describes only aggressive short-covering in thin trade with Brazil on holiday, which read alone would be REFUSE.

known_cause: Crop concerns from dry weather in Brazil and Vietnam sent arabica to a two-year high, with fund buying adding to it.
notes: Intraday market report; its date (2024-04-17) is inferred from the prices it quotes, not read from the page. The cause is a general condition, not one event that day.

known_cause: Exchange-monitored arabica stocks rose to a one-year high, easing supply concerns and setting off selling by holders of long positions.
notes: Closing report dated 2024-05-02: July arabica -9.90 cents (-4.58%, against -4.75% in the price series). A second daily report of 2024-05-03 agrees.

known_cause: A reaction to the US tariff package and China's retaliation, part of a broad sell-off; the report says coffee's own fundamentals had not changed.
notes: Report dated 2025-04-04: May/25 -1,955 points, which is -5.07% and matches. Reports for the neighbouring sessions give the same trade-war explanation.

known_cause: A weather service reported no rain in Minas Gerais in the week to 12 July, which set off fund short-covering, on top of the announced 50% US tariff on Brazilian imports.
notes: Intraday market report; its date (2025-07-14) is inferred from the rainfall week and prices it quotes. It shows +4.03% during the session against +5.93% at the close.

known_cause: After a four-month high arabica dropped on profit-taking, with the report also citing a stronger dollar and more favourable weather for Brazil's arabica crop.
notes: CHECK: borderline. Report dated 2026-01-28: Mar/26 -16.25 cents (-4.4%). The first reason given is profit-taking; the dollar and weather are named but vaguely (the real moved 'modestly'). Read strictly this is REFUSE.

known_cause: Forecasts of a cold air mass moving into Brazil's coffee regions revived frost fears and forced short-covering, with tight exchange stocks, harvest delays and El Nino worries behind it.
notes: Report dated 2026-07-07: the July contract rose more than 16%. A real move, confirmed by two other reports of 2026-07-07, one calling it the largest one-day gain since 2000.
